Getting started

  1. Click the link above. You will need to be signed in to a free Google account.
  2. Choose Make a copy when Google asks. The copy is saved in your own Google Drive and is private to you.
  3. On the Candle tab, set Weigh in to grams or ounces.
  4. Enter the water weight of your jar. The wax and fragrance weights are calculated from it.
How to weigh your jar. Put the empty jar on your scale and zero it. Fill it with water to the height you want the wax to reach, leaving room for the lid. Enter that water weight in the sheet.

The three tabs

  • Candle — your jar and fragrance percentage. Wax and fragrance oil, per candle and per batch.
  • Costs & Price — your materials, fees and margin. Cost per candle and selling price.
  • Reference — every assumption, where to change it, and what each term means.

Before you start

Fragrance load and fragrance content are different numbers. 20 g of fragrance in 200 g of wax is a 10% load and a 9.09% content. Select whichever one your recipe or wax spec sheet uses. The calculator shows both.
Adding 40% to your cost does not give you a 40% margin. It gives about 29%. Enter the margin you want and the sheet calculates the price that delivers it after your selling fees.
This calculator does not choose your wick. Wick size depends on your wax, fragrance load, dye and the shape of your jar, and it is confirmed by burning a test candle and watching the melt pool. Use the printable Burn Test Log included with this download to record what you try.

Cell colors

  • Cream cells — enter your own numbers here.
  • Gray cells — calculated automatically. Do not type in these.
  • Blue cells — editable assumptions. Change them if your materials or process differ.
